advice.instructions:
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:
- "proposals": a list, one entry per proposal id above, each {"id": the proposal id, "conflict": "conflict" or "no_conflict" or "not_stated" (whether it conflicts with the mandate; not_stated when the mandate says nothing on its article; never invent a position that is not on record), "basis": "on_record" when the positions on record above state it, or "inferred" when it rests on other text, "basis_quote": for an inferred entry the exact line it rests on, copied from the text above, "stance": "accept" or "reject" or "counter", "wording": the middle-ground text for a counter (empty otherwise), "reasons": a list of the PAR- and POS- ids your advice rests on}.
- "trades": a list of {"give": a proposal id, "get": a proposal id}.
- "approach": a list of the party ids to approach.
- "alignment": a list, one entry per article id of the excerpt, each {"article": the id, "aligned": the party ids aligned with the party you advise on it, "opposed": the party ids opposed, "basis" and "basis_quote" as for a proposal}; a party with no position on record on the article is in neither list.
- "state": a list, one entry per article id of the excerpt and per article of the previous round no longer in this round, each {"article": the id, "state": "closed" or "dropped" or "bracketed" or "new" or "binding"}, binding meaning an earlier concession of the party you advise binds it.

stepwise.order_note: D-756 item 6 (N3), lane/neg-improve: generated_first, the order S0 shipped with and the default, asks the generated changes step first and shows its line to every later step, so a refused changes ends the proposal's chain. choice_first asks the choice steps (stance per touched position, red line, open point) first from the choice_first templates, none of which shows {changes}, then the generated steps (changes; wording when the open point is yes); a refused generated step drops only its own field and is counted with its reason. Read by neg_advisor.stepwise_advice; changing it changes the prompts file's config digest, so a run under choice_first needs its own prompts build and seal.
stepwise.stance_context_note: D-756 item 5 (P8), lane/neg-improve: the stance step's context is chosen per prompt at build time (neg_advisor.py build --stance-contexts full,trimmed), never here, so one prompts file carries both arms side by side, each prompt and answers row marked stance_context. full (or none marked) is the order's own stance template; trimmed is stance_trimmed above: the proposal's text, the one position and the persona's red lines on record. No fate forecast is in the chain; one added later keeps the whole item.
stepwise.optional_note: lane/neg-optional (Seckin 19 November 2026 01:23, the optional ideas of D-756): five switches, each off as shipped and read by neg_advisor.optional_switches when the chain runs; off, the chain asks what it asked before. A run under any of them needs its own prompts build and seal. fate_forecast (P2), conflict_question two_checks (C2), quote_grounding (P6), auditor_band (P5, needs quote_grounding), conditional_accept (C3). stepwise.fate_note: P2: the forecast is marked fate_basis inferred (D-711) and never writes the conflict field. fate_precedence stance keeps the chain's stance and sets the fate beside it; fate sets the stance from fate_stance (the plan's M4 pairs: kept accept, changed counter, removed reject), the chain's stance kept as stance_from_fate, so M5 can be read beside. Judged against the constant answers, not against zero (all-reject gives M4 0.480).
stepwise.two_checks_note: C2: conflict_question two_checks asks touches and holds in place of the stance question; oppose is touches yes and holds no, anything else two_checks_otherwise; the oppose margin is the smaller of p(yes) minus p(no) on touches and p(no) minus p(yes) on holds.
stepwise.quote_note: P6: asked after an oppose, the position's sentences numbered by form (at most 9; more, or none, is not asked and counted); 0 sends the oppose back to quote_none_stance; a refused answer keeps the oppose ungrounded, counted, never ending the chain.
stepwise.auditor_note: P5: auditor_band [low, high) on the persona's oppose margin; a position inside it is grounded as in P6 and, when a sentence is chosen, asked of the second family (system_audit, its declared answers); supported flips the proposal from no_conflict to conflict (an accept becomes reject). No cue word is read (WORDS-A).
stepwise.conditional_note: C3: conditional_accept, when declared, is {"label": "conditional", "counts_as": "accept"}: counts_as from D-748 (Seckin 18:46 and 18:48: a hedged support with a proviso is labelled accept), written before any read; the piece keeps answered conditional on the position. The carry-forward while the condition holds (open item 158) is not modelled.
stepwise.compare_note: C4 (lane/neg-conflict-fix, D-806, docs/loop/stages/NEG_CONFLICT_FIX_REPORT.md): conflict_question compare asks, per touched position, this one question in place of the stance question: what the position asks for set against what the proposal would do, both rounds shown, since most positions were put on record before the proposal's text existed and cannot hold an attitude toward it. Each answer counts as its declared stance (written before any read, never from labels); the piece keeps answered beside it; the oppose margin is the margin toward against. Each label's first token on the producer's tokenizer is a whole word (against 68749, fits 29222, aside 28512), where oppose was scored on the fragment op (453). Off as shipped (conflict_question stance); a run under it needs its own prompts build (neg_advisor.py build --config) and seal.
stepwise.limit_note: R2 (lane/neg-round2-candidate, D-814 round 2, docs/loop/stages/NEG_ROUND2_CANDIDATE.md): limit_read true reads each persona position not marked a red line once per item, before any proposal, with limit (the position alone, no proposal shown), over limit_answers (exactly one counting as a limit, declared before any read, never from labels); each proposal a position read as a limit applies to is then asked limit_cross, and a yes makes it a conflict as a marked red line's yes does. The piece keeps limit_hit and limit_lines marked limit_basis inferred, apart from red_line_hit; the reply keeps limit_reads. A refused read or crossing is no limit and no crossing, counted, never ending a chain. Composes with conflict_question stance, two_checks or compare (C4), either order and either stance context. Each label's first token on the producer's tokenizer is a whole word (firm 8802, wish 81099). Off as shipped; a run under it needs its own prompts build (neg_advisor.py build --config) and seal.

stepwise.reason_text:
A proposal on the table in article {article} ({title}):
{proposal}

The advice for the party you advise on it: {stance}.

Write exactly two lines and nothing else:
Mechanism: how this proposal would work if it were adopted as written.
Effect: what it would change for the party you advise.
stepwise.reason_note: #311 (same lane, D-845): reason_field true asks this generated step after each proposal's stance; Python reads the two lines by their heads (Mechanism:, Effect:) into the piece's reason; a reply without both is refused with no_mechanism or no_effect, counted like every refused step, and only this field is dropped. Recorded and reported, never a bar figure. Off as shipped.
stepwise.trade_note: #3 (same lane, D-846): the stepwise chain's reply held no trades though 21 of 64 C4 items declare trades on record. trade_read true asks, per declared trade of the advised party whose give and get are both on the table, this one CHOICE-A question; a kept trade is offered again in the reply's trades, every read kept in trade_reads marked inferred. First tokens on the producer's tokenizer are whole words (keep 13096, drop 6719). Off as shipped.
stepwise.changes_id_echo_note: R3b (same lane): the changes template shows {proposal_id}: {proposal}, and the model copies the line with the id in front (c4pilot_1: 111 of 112 not_in_the_proposal refusals; c4val_1: 175 of 176). changes_id_echo true reads a changes answer starting with exactly the proposal id the prompt showed and a colon without that id, checks the rest word for word as before, and marks the step id_echo.
